approach: Root cause: a failed check's record keeps the last 200 lines of the log whatever those lines are. For a CI log those lines are GitHub Actions post-job cleanup, so they push out the test runner's `failures:` / `panicked at` section. This happens at three sites: the local run in checks.rs (~533), `with_failure_detail` (checks.rs ~361) and `detail_from_job_logs` (gh/client.rs ~293). Fix: add one shared `checks::failure_section(text, max_lines) -> String`. It (1) cuts the text at the first runner cleanup line (`Post job cleanup`, `Post Run `, `Cleaning up orphan processes`, with an optional `##[group]` prefix); (2) if what is left fits in max_lines, keeps it; (3) otherwise keeps the last max_lines lines when that window holds a runner marker (`failures:`, `panicked at`, `---- … stdout ----`, `test result: FAILED`) or when the text has no marker at all (today's behavior); (4) otherwise keeps max_lines lines from the earliest marker; (5) applies the FAILED_TAIL_BYTES cap. `client.rs` applies it per job log so one job's cleanup cannot cut another job's log. `with_failure_detail` applies it to the body and keeps a leading `failing units:` line, which verify.rs reads. Redaction is unchanged and still runs on the kept text. Passing checks are untouched. No record or schema change. Revision: criterion 5's demonstration now names its seam and what fails without the behavior; the rest of the plan is unchanged.

decisions.choice: One shared selector `failure_section` in checks.rs, called by the local run, with_failure_detail and detail_from_job_logs.
decisions.reason: All three sites build the record from the same line-tail rule, so fixing it once keeps them from drifting apart.

rejected.why: Fixes the CI path only. The local run keeps the same tail rule and with_failure_detail stays unprotected.

rejected.option: Store the failures section via failed_test_names output
rejected.why: failed_test_names yields names only, no assertion text, and returns nothing for an xtask panic.

decisions.choice: Hybrid window: keep today's last-N-lines when it already holds a marker or when there is no marker; jump to the earliest marker only when markers exist and the tail window has none.
decisions.reason: Existing tests (shard_log `== shard` line, run/tests.rs 200-line test, 'build broke' with no marker) keep their output, and a log with no marker and no cleanup is unchanged, as criterion 4 requires.

rejected.option: Always start at the earliest marker
rejected.why: Drops the `== shard k/n` line and `Running` context that existing tests and failing-units extraction rely on, and changes output for logs that were fine.

decisions.choice: Cut at the first cleanup marker per job log, not on the joined multi-job text.
decisions.reason: detail_from_job_logs joins several shard logs; a cut at the first marker of the joined text would drop later jobs' failures.

rejected.option: Strip once on the joined text
rejected.why: Loses the second and later shards' failing output.

decisions.choice: In with_failure_detail, set aside a leading `failing units:` line, section the rest with max_lines-1, then put the line back.
decisions.reason: verify.rs reads that first line; the client output is the prefix plus up to 200 lines, so a plain 200-line cut would drop the prefix.

rejected.option: Leave with_failure_detail as a plain call
rejected.why: It would keep dropping the prefix line for a full-length log.

files.purpose: Add failure_section, is_cleanup_line, is_runner_marker; use them in run_check (failed branch) and with_failure_detail (keeping the `failing units:` first line); add unit tests.

steps: In checks.rs add `is_cleanup_line(line)` (trim, strip a leading `##[group]`, then starts_with `Post job cleanup`, `Post Run ` or `Cleaning up orphan processes`) and `is_runner_marker(line)` (trimmed == `failures:`, contains `panicked at`, starts with `---- ` and ends with ` stdout ----`, or starts with `test result: FAILED`).

Add `pub fn failure_section(text: &str, max_lines: usize) -> String` next to tail_lines: cut at the first cleanup line (keep a final newline); return `tail(...)` of the whole text if it fits; else the last max_lines lines if that window has a marker or the text has none; else max_lines lines from the first marker; always finish with `tail(.., FAILED_TAIL_BYTES)`. Doc comment names the root cause (the old rule kept the last N lines whatever they were). Keep `tail_lines` and its test.

Replace `tail(&tail_lines(&output, FAILED_TAIL_LINES), FAILED_TAIL_BYTES)` in run_check (failed branch only) with `failure_section(&output, FAILED_TAIL_LINES)`. In with_failure_detail, split off a leading FAILING_UNITS_PREFIX line, call failure_section(rest, FAILED_TAIL_LINES - 1) when it was present (FAILED_TAIL_LINES otherwise), and put the line back. Redaction stays first.

In gh/client.rs detail_from_job_logs, for each readable job push the `== name` header when more than one is readable, then `failure_section(log, FAILED_TAIL_LINES)`; cap the joined text again with tail_lines and tail so the total stays bounded. Leave name extraction on the full plain log untouched.

Add the checks.rs tests: pure `failure_section` cases (cleanup over 200 lines after a failures section; no marker and no cleanup equals the old tail; marker in window unchanged; marker above a marker-free window; passing-check output untouched), the `run_script` local-run test, and the with_failure_detail prefix test.
Add the gh/tests.rs tests for detail_from_job_logs (single shard xtask panic with cleanup; two shards each with cleanup).
Update the doc comment in ci_result.rs and add the CHANGELOG bullet under [Unreleased] → Fixed, stating only what the diff does.

Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p athena-core checks`, `cargo test -p athena-core gh`, then `cargo test --locked`. Confirm the new behavior tests fail on the base by running them with the non-test source changes temporarily reverted (git stash of the non-test source files).

risks.risk: A cleanup marker string printed by a test itself would cut the log early.
risks.mitigation: Markers are specific (`Post job cleanup`, `Post Run `, `Cleaning up orphan processes`) and matched at the start of a trimmed line after an optional `##[group]` prefix; a test pins the exact forms.

risks.risk: Real Actions logs may show cleanup in forms not guessed here.
risks.mitigation: The hybrid fallback goes to the earliest runner marker when the tail window has none, so an unknown cleanup shape does not hide the failing section while `failures:` or `panicked at` is present. Keep the marker list in one place.

risks.risk: Jumping to the earliest marker drops later output (a second failing binary) beyond max_lines.
risks.mitigation: The cap is the existing 200 lines and 64 KiB; the jump happens only when the tail window has no marker; failed_tests still comes from the full log.

risks.risk: run/tests.rs is a listed deliverable but needs no edit; its 200-line test is unaffected.
risks.mitigation: Leave it unchanged, say so in the producer summary, and run it under cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: Prefix handling changes a full-length reused detail from 200 lines to prefix plus 199.
risks.mitigation: A new test pins it; before, the prefix line was dropped for logs of 200 or more lines.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff: `failure_section` is defined in checks.rs with a doc comment naming the root cause; its call sites are run_check, with_failure_detail and detail_from_job_logs; the CHANGELOG entry states the change.
demonstrations.observes: One new function; the three `tail(&tail_lines(...))` sites are replaced by calls to it; the doc comment says the old rule kept the last N lines regardless of content so cleanup text displaced the failing section.

demonstrations.method: Two new tests in checks.rs `mod tests`. (a) `failure_section_drops_cleanup_and_keeps_failing_section` calls `failure_section` on cargo output (`failures:`, `---- t stdout ----`, `thread 't' panicked at … assertion failed`, `test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed`) followed by 250 `Post job cleanup`-style lines; asserts the test name and assertion text are present and `Post job cleanup` is absent. (b) `a_failed_local_run_keeps_the_failing_section_not_trailing_cleanup` uses the existing `run_script(&sh_spec(...))` helper (checks.rs ~736), which calls production `run_check`; the script echoes the failing section, then 250 `Post job cleanup.` lines, and exits 1; asserts `output_tail` has the panic text and no cleanup.
demonstrations.observes: Both tests pass with the change. On the base commit they fail: the last 200 lines are all cleanup, so the test name is absent and `Post job cleanup` is present.
demonstrations.fails_without: The kept output holds only cleanup lines: the test-name assertion fails and the no-cleanup assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `checks::failure_section` (added by plan step 2) and `checks::run_check` via the existing `run_script` helper (exists, read in checks.rs). The fixture is the shell script text passed to sh_spec; no double.

demonstrations.method: New test in gh/tests.rs using the existing `stamped` helper: a CI log with no `Running`/`Doc-tests` line and no `test … FAILED` lines (xtask-style panic `thread 'repin' panicked at xtask/src/…: pin mismatch`, `test result: FAILED`) followed by 250 stamped `Post job cleanup.` and `Cleaning up orphan processes` lines. Call `detail_from_job_logs` with `[("test (shard 1)", "failure", Some(log))]`; assert output_tail contains the panic message, has no `Post job cleanup`, and failed_tests is empty. A second case with two shard logs, each ending in cleanup, asserts both panic messages survive.
demonstrations.observes: output_tail holds the panic message and no cleanup lines. On the base the 200-line tail is all cleanup and the panic text is missing.
demonstrations.fails_without: The panic message is absent from output_tail and cleanup lines are present, so both assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `gh::client::detail_from_job_logs`, input a plain `(name, conclusion, Option<String>)` slice, already called by existing tests (gh/tests.rs ~680). The `stamped` fixture helper exists (gh/tests.rs ~376). No new seam.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in checks.rs: `failure_section` on 300 numbered lines with no marker and no cleanup equals `tail_lines(text, 200)` plus the byte cap; a marker inside the last 200 lines gives the same output as `tail_lines`; a marker far above a marker-free window starts the section at that marker; a with_failure_detail test with a `failing units:` first line plus 300 lines keeps the prefix as first line; a passing run's output is still the byte tail. Existing tests also run: `a_failed_run_keeps_its_last_200_lines_and_a_passing_run_its_byte_tail`, `a_reused_failed_check_takes_the_redacted_names_and_tail_and_logs_the_names`, `red_reused_run_records_failing_tests_and_log_tail`, the run/tests.rs 200-line test (~3481-3499), and the verify.rs tests reading `failing units:`.
demonstrations.observes: All pass; marker-free, cleanup-free output equals the old tail, and the prefix line survives.
demonstrations.fails_without: A selector that always started at the earliest marker, or always cut by line count, would change the old outputs and fail the existing exact-line assertions and the prefix test.
demonstrations.seam: Production `checks::failure_section`, `checks::with_failure_detail` and `checks::run_check` (via run_script). Existing fixtures; no double. The new tests are added by plan step 5.
